title: Cyber Hygiene
briefing: A phishing simulation run by IT had a 19% click rate. 14% of servers are more than 60 days behind on critical patches. The IT Manager, Mei Lin, has a budget request for 120,000 that nobody has approved.
Your team's assessment of route planning (from last quarter) found no offline fallback. Pull it together into a recommendation.

context.text: The Risk Committee chair has started asking why the risk team's reports never contain bad news.

evidence.title: Phishing simulation results
evidence.body: 1,240 staff tested. Clicked: 236 (19%). Entered credentials: 61 (5%). Reported the email: 84 (7%). Finance and dispatch had the highest click rates.

evidence.title: Patch status
evidence.body: Critical patches older than 60 days: 14% of servers, including the depot scanning gateway. Policy target: 0% after 30 days.

evidence.title: Access controls
evidence.body: Multi-factor login for administrators only. Email and the route-planning portal use passwords alone. Backups are taken nightly; the last restore test was 18 months ago.

evidence.title: IT budget request (unapproved)
evidence.body: 120,000: MFA for all staff (35,000), patch automation (40,000), restore testing and an offline dispatch fallback (45,000).

questions.prompt: Which gaps most raise the likelihood or impact of a ransomware outage?

options.label: No MFA on email and the route-planning portal while 5% of staff hand over credentials
Critical patches 60+ days old on 14% of servers
Backups never test-restored in 18 months, and no offline dispatch
The 19% click rate on its own
options.feedback: Clicks matter mainly because credentials are then enough to log in: the MFA gap is the root.

options.label: Only 7% reported the phishing email
options.feedback: Worth improving, but a weaker driver than the three control gaps.

questions.prompt: What do you recommend? Your authority as team lead is 150,000.

options.label: Approve the 120,000 package, phased: MFA and the restore test in the first month, patch automation and the offline fallback next
options.feedback: Within your authority, ordered by risk reduction per unit of time.

options.label: More phishing training; revisit the budget next year
options.feedback: Training helps a little, but the control gaps remain open.

schedules.description: Ransomware encrypts the depot scanning gateway and spreads to route planning

options.label: Accept the risk: we have antivirus and nightly backups
options.feedback: Untested backups are a hope, not a control.

schedules.description: Ransomware encrypts the depot scanning gateway and spreads to route planning
Stolen email credentials are used to export a customer contact list

questions.prompt: An outage of route planning costs about 450,000. The package is judged to cut the annual probability from 25% to 5%. Over one year, is it worth it?

options.label: Yes: expected loss falls by about 90,000 a year (from 112,500 to 22,500), so it pays back in under two years, before counting reputation
No: 120,000 is more than the 112,500 expected loss
options.feedback: Compare the reduction over the controls' life, not one year's cost against one year's loss.

options.label: Yes: it saves 450,000
options.feedback: That treats the worst case as certain.

questions.prompt: How do you make sure the gaps actually close?

options.label: Create tracked actions with owners and dates, add MFA coverage and patch age as KRIs, and report progress monthly to the committee
Leave it to Mei Lin; IT knows best
Check again at the annual review
options.feedback: A year is too long for exposures this live.

questions.prompt: Dispatch supervisors object that MFA will slow them down at shift change. Your response:

options.label: Pilot it with one depot using app approval, measure the time added, and adjust before rollout
options.feedback: Takes the concern seriously and answers it with evidence.

options.label: Mandate it anyway: security comes first
options.feedback: Probably right on substance, but forced rollouts invite workarounds.

options.label: Exempt dispatch
options.feedback: Dispatch had one of the highest click rates.

lesson: Fix the controls that turn a click into an outage: MFA, patching and tested recovery. Quantify the reduction, then track the actions until they close.
